the_crux_question.question: Is intrinsic NULL valid for an ALLOCATABLE component? Two of the three suspected compiler defects depended entirely on this. If NULL were not permitted for an allocatable component, the fixtures would have been INVALID, LFortran's rejection CORRECT, and this a blocking test defect rather than two compiler defects.
the_crux_question.why_it_needed_asking: The rules differ by component kind - for a POINTER component NULL gives disassociated status - and it is easy to assume the allocatable case by analogy. An ICE and a SIGSEGV are crashes, not diagnoses, so the source had to be proven conforming before attributing either to a defect.
the_crux_question.resolution: 7.5.10 p6 EXPLICITLY permits intrinsic NULL for allocatable constructor expressions and states the component 'has a status of unallocated'. NULL(MOLD=...) is valid via 16.9.155 p3/p4/p7.
the_crux_question.outcome: The fixtures are conforming; both ICEs are genuine LFortran defects.

source_derivations_independently_confirm.conforming_array_bound_mapping: source(1:3) maps to component values(-1:1) as 11, 13, 17 - the component keeps its DECLARED bounds rather than inheriting the source's. This was flagged as the detail most easily got backwards and is correct.
source_derivations_independently_confirm.numeric_conversion: Real 4.0 to an integer component gives 4. The value is EXACTLY REPRESENTABLE in binary floating point, so no rounding ambiguity arises - important because reals are approximations under 7.4.3.
source_derivations_independently_confirm.character_deferred_length: A CHARACTER(3) source gives an allocated component with LEN 3 and values QRS / LMN. LEN is asserted explicitly and both values are nonblank, guarding the blank-padding trap.
source_derivations_independently_confirm.keyword_order: right=13, left=11 yields left 11 and right 13; the components hold DISTINCT values, without which the order-independence claim would be untestable.

non_vacuity_by_mutation.decisive_check_for_defaults: REMOVING THE OMITTED DEFAULTS FAILS. This is the critical test for a default-initialization fixture: if the default were a zero-equivalent value, the test would pass on a processor that ignores default initialization entirely. Defaults (11,13) and override (11,29) are non-default-equivalent.

The reviewer confirmed these read NO bounds or values, so no undefined state is observed, and that each establishes a meaningful contrast rather than resting on the default state alone.

integrator_corrective_action.issue: The packet added a new assertion to the PRE-EXISTING sibling module tests/test_constructor_declaration_fixtures.py requiring the rendered 7.5.10 view to say 'Catalogue source review: stale.', and emitted the view itself with 'stale'. Both are only true BEFORE integration. After the integrator renewed the catalogue review, the view correctly reads 'reviewed' and the gate failed.
integrator_corrective_action.root_cause: AUTHORS CANNOT RECORD REVIEWS - --record-* is integrator-only - so a fixture author only ever observes the stale state. Encoding that state in a test assertion or a rendered artefact bakes in a value that FLIPS at integration by design.
integrator_corrective_action.why_it_matters: 7.5.10 is rendered by TWO generators (generate_constructor_declaration_fixtures.py and this packet's generate_structure_constructor_effect_fixtures.py), so the assertion lived in a module the packet did not own. The packet legitimately updated that module's pending count from 76 to 61, but also added the review-state assertion, which was not legitimate.
integrator_corrective_action.remedy: Corrected the rendered view to 'reviewed' and the sibling assertion to expect 'reviewed', matching the post-integration truth. The pending-count update to 61 was correct and retained.
integrator_corrective_action.generalised_rule: A fixture packet must NOT assert the catalogue review state, in a test or in a rendered artefact. That state is stale during authoring and reviewed after integration, so any hardcoded expectation is wrong in one of the two phases. Render the view AFTER recording the review, and assert only content the packet actually owns.
